providers.detail: Live provider APIs and published price lists. Every price carries a source and last_verified; nothing is published without one.

matrix.detail: Recomputed from providers + specs on each run.

spot.detail: Aggregated from this run's usable provider list prices (stale and out-of-date fallback prices excluded). on_demand_low/avg/high span the providers listing each GPU. Spot and 1-/3-year committed bands appear only where a provider publishes that rate, and each saving is measured against on-demand over the SAME providers (*_vs_ondemand). No bid/ask: nothing trades against a list price; traded quotes are in prediction_markets.

historical.detail: Monthly min/average/max per GPU, aggregated from the daily per-provider price record over the provider set tracked today, excluding stale, carried-forward and fallback prices. The month-on-month change (change_pct) is computed only over providers that priced the GPU in both months and whose method did not change in between, so a provider joining, leaving or returning (listed per month) cannot read as a price move. Replaces a series that spliced a hand-seeded era onto live figures: it showed H100 doubling in a month and drove a false 202% year-on-year rise into the volatility panel, which then labelled six GPUs 'tightening' while prices were flat or falling. It starts at 2026-05 because live scraping replaced hardcoded seed prices on 2026-04-30 and nothing before that is comparable -- short and true rather than long and spliced.

summary.detail: Recomputed from matrix, providers and indicators.

tco.detail: Cloud rates track live provider averages; includes commitment break-even (formerly a separate reservations dataset). Power/colo/staff inputs are overridable in the Scenario Builder.

inference.detail: OpenRouter. Token and request volumes are the published daily rankings figures; per-provider prices, quantization, context and uptime come from /api/v1/models/{slug}/endpoints. The roster was previously copied by hand and went stale between edits; it is now whatever the rankings say that day. Trend history is accumulated here one observation per run, so it starts short and lengthens.

news.detail: Google News RSS. Dates are as published.

sentiment.detail: Reddit, HuggingFace and GitHub APIs. Composite scores are our own weighting.

indicators.detail: NVDA/AMD prices, 52-week range and YTD (vs the prior year-end close) are live from Yahoo Finance. AI capex (ai_capex_bn) is derived each run as the sum of the latest management capex guidance for AMZN, CRWV, GOOGL, META, MSFT (guidance as of 2026-11-10; curated with citations). GPU market size (gpu_market_size_bn) is an editorial estimate, last set 2026-07-28, not refreshed by the pipeline. Lead times are curated.

sustainability.detail: Per-GPU energy, carbon and water computed from specs.tdp_watts each run, using the five constants in sustainability.assumptions (sustained load 82% of TDP, US grid 0.40 kg CO2e/kWh, Nordic 0.045, water 1.8 L/kWh, embodied 200 kg/kW). Previously a hand-written table that covered 9 of 17 GPUs and had drifted from specs -- GB200 carried the 2700W superchip TDP against a per-GPU price, overstating its power and carbon 2.25x. Embodied carbon is an order-of-magnitude estimate; the rest is arithmetic. Provider PUE and grid figures alongside this are from published sustainability reports.

supplychain.detail: Export-control timeline is public record; vendor risk scores are editorial. Regional unit-count inventories have been removed.

regional.detail: Same Azure VM SKU priced across regions via the Retail Prices API. Replaces modelled regional market share.

modelfit.detail: Open-weights models from the current demand leaderboard, sized against live GPU prices. Parameter counts are the exact totals from each model's HuggingFace safetensors index; layers, KV heads and head dim come from its config.json. VRAM = (weights + KV cache) x 1.2: a 20% overhead on weights plus KV for activations and fragmentation -- that 20% is the only assumption. KV cache is fp16 at every precision. FP8 options are limited to GPUs with native FP8 tensor cores (Ada, Hopper, Blackwell, CDNA 3). MoE models hold every expert in VRAM, so weights use total parameters while the active count is reported separately. Break-even throughput solves for the output tokens/sec a rig must sustain to beat the cheapest API route for the same model, so no throughput figure is invented.

volatility.detail: Realized volatility, drawdown and trend per GPU, computed from the daily market average across the providers tracked today. Previously computed from the monthly series, which after being rebuilt on one comparable basis holds four points -- three returns. Annualized volatility is only reported where at least 20 daily returns stand behind it, and the observation count is published with every figure. Stale and fallback prices are not in the record, and any daily return spanning a methodology change of a provider in the average is left out (returns_excluded).

changelog.detail: Price movements between consecutive refreshes. Moves over 100% are flagged for review rather than published as signal.

prediction_markets.detail: Live order books: Kalshi trade API and Polymarket Gamma API. Implied prices are read off the quoted ladder/brackets (median of the market-implied distribution) -- no model of ours. Both venues settle against the Ornn GPU compute index, which is not the same basket as our provider list-price average, so the two series are related but not directly comparable.

price_history.detail: Each provider's published price per GPU, per day. Backfilled from the git history of data.json -- every commit is an exact record of what was published that day -- and appended once per run thereafter. The change feed was not used: it only logs moves of 3% or more, so a series rebuilt from it drifts. Only usable prices are recorded: stale, carried forward more than 48h, or hardcoded fallback prices are not observations and are left out (and purged from days recorded before that rule). Days on which our scraper read the wrong column are dropped. Windows containing one of this pipeline's own scraper corrections are flagged, because those moves are not the market.

ai_analysis.detail: Language-model commentary over the snapshot of this data. Not a forecast. Each block carries its generation date; blocks older than 7 days are flagged on the page.

term_structure.detail: On-demand and committed rates for the top-tier GPUs, read from each provider's published price list (AWS Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, Azure reservations, GCP committed use, Lambda 1-Click Cluster reservations, Together reserved clusters, DigitalOcean 12-month reserved). Discounts compare a commitment with the SAME provider's on-demand rate; multi-node cluster reservations are listed but kept out of the discount medians. The spread-over-time series uses a fixed set of providers. Providers that only quote commitments through sales (CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe, Oracle, RunPod, Vultr) are not shown as offering one.

reserved_market.detail: Short-term capacity, hyperscaler discount schedules and regional prices are read from provider price pages and APIs each run. The Ornn index and GetDeploying weekly medians are third-party market data (GetDeploying CC BY 4.0). The evidence timeline is curated by hand from dated public reports.

contracts.method: Curated, citation-backed list of large multi-year compute/capacity contracts. Every number was read from the cited url (or a second url named in the note) on 2026-11-12. confidence: 'disclosed' = stated by a party (press release, blog or SEC filing); 'reported' = not disclosed by the companies, taken from reputable press as noted. Most values are 'up to' ceilings subject to delivery, availability and termination conditions, not guaranteed payments. term_years is the stated term where there is one; for CoreWeave rows it is the span from signing to the stated end date, noted per row. Implied $/GPU-hr is computed only when value, term and GPU count for the same contract are all disclosed or reported: value / (gpus x 8760 x years), or monthly fee x 12 / (gpus x 8760). It assumes every GPU is billed for the whole term (deliveries are often phased, which would raise the true rate) and includes everything the contract bundles (networking, storage, CPUs, power, data center, services), so it is an upper bound on pure GPU cost. Rows with an implied price have confidence 'estimate'; their inputs are disclosed figures. GPU counts are never inferred from MW. Colocation leases (Fluidstack rows) are power/space, not compute, and must not be compared with GPU-hour prices. Rows for the same buyer and seller can overlap (CoreWeave-OpenAI tranches sum to the ~$22.4B CoreWeave reported; the Nscale Narvik row may be inside the Nscale $43.8B aggregate).
